newsitem.title: CHINA: China city to regulate property management.
newsitem.headline: China city to regulate property management.

text.p: China's booming industrial centre of Shanghai has issued a set of provisional rules aimed at standardising the city's property management firms, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.

The rules, which took effect on September 1, were intended to tighten control over property management companies and pave the way for a rating system for all Chinese and foreign-funded property management firms, Xinhua said.
Businesses that refused to abide by the new rules would have their licence revoked, it said.
The number of property management companies in Shanghai had been growing at an annual rate of 80 percent since 1992 and currently stood at 1,400, it said.
The rapid growth of the sector had been accompanied by a rise in complaints from residents unhappy with building management, it said.
